mainTopic: Women and חמץ/מצה, the expounding of כל and כי כל, and when permitted food joins forbidden food
overview: The גמרא explains why the Torah needed an extra word to forbid women from eating חמץ: the verse links חמץ with מצה, and women are exempt from מצה as a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. Now that women are included in the חמץ prohibition, רבי אליעזר holds that the same link makes them obligated to eat מצה by Torah law. The גמרא asks why the word כל includes women rather than a mixture of חמץ (עירובו). It answers that a verse about eaters adds more eaters, and it adds foods only when no eaters are left to add, as with חלב. The רבנן, who do not expound כל, learn women from the fuller phrase כי כל. The גמרא then asks why רבי אליעזר does not use כי כל to include עירובו, since a ברייתא about שאור on the מזבח shows he expounds it, and this question remains a קשיא. Next, רבי יוחנן teaches that permitted food never joins forbidden food to make up the minimum amount, except for a נזיר. זעירי adds שאור on the מזבח as another exception, following רבי אליעזר, and a challenge to this begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why a special source is needed to include women in the prohibition of חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it is not obvious that women are forbidden to eat חמץ. The verse links the חמץ prohibition with the מצה obligation, and women are exempt from מצה because it is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. So we might have exempted them from חמץ too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the verse says 'Do not eat חמץ with it; seven days eat מצות with it,' anyone who must eat מצה is also forbidden to eat חמץ. Women are not obligated to eat מצה, because it is a positive מצוה tied to a time. So I might say they are also not forbidden to eat חמץ. Therefore the verse teaches us that they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier 'פשיטא' (isn't this obvious?) by showing why we might have thought women are allowed to eat חמץ. That is why a special word was needed to include them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally women are bound by every לא תעשה, so including them in a prohibition seems unnecessary. But here the Torah places the חמץ prohibition right next to the מצה obligation in one verse, which could suggest the two always go together. Since women are exempt from מצה, we might have thought they are exempt from חמץ too.

keyTerms.meaning: It could have entered your mind to say: what we might have wrongly thought
'Get up and eat מצה': the positive command to eat מצה
'Do not eat חמץ': the prohibition against eating leaven
A positive מצוה tied to a specific time; women are generally exempt
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Women are normally obligated in every prohibition (לא תעשה). The only reason we might have exempted them here is that the חמץ prohibition is linked in the verse to the מצה obligation.

phrases.english: It could have entered your mind to say:
since it is written
"You shall not eat leavened bread with it;
seven days you shall eat matzos with it,"
anyone who is included in "arise, eat matzah"
is included in "do not eat leaven."
And these women,
since they are not included in "arise, eat matzah,"
because it is a positive commandment
that is caused by time (it is),

phrases.aramaic: — אֵימָא בְּבַל תֹּאכַל חָמֵץ נָמֵי לֵיתַנְהוּ,
phrases.english: I might say they are also not included in "do not eat leaven."
So the verse teaches us (that they are included).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier 'פשיטא' challenge (on the previous amud) against including women in the חמץ prohibition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא explanation: shows why the teaching is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse ties חמץ to מצה, so women exempt from מצה would be exempt from חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word כל teaches that women are forbidden to eat חמץ despite their exemption from מצה.

steps.title: Women are therefore also obligated to eat מצה
steps.stepSummary: Now that women are included in the חמץ prohibition, the same link works in reverse: women are also obligated to eat מצה, as רבי אליעזר holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that women have been included in the prohibition of eating חמץ, they are also included in the obligation of eating מצה, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a new conclusion from the previous step: the link between חמץ and מצה now makes women obligated in מצה. It is also setting up the next step, which brings רבי אליעזר's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the link between the two commands seemed to exempt women from חמץ. Now that women are clearly included in the חמץ prohibition, the same link runs the other way and brings them into the מצה obligation. This overrides the usual rule exempting women from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא.

keyTerms.meaning: They were included (by a word in the verse)
The מצוה of eating מצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that women are obligated to eat מצה on the night of פסח, even though it is a time-bound positive מצוה.

phrases.english: And now that they have been included
in "do not eat leaven,"
they are also included in eating matzah,
in accordance with Rabbi (Eliezer).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאִתְרַבּוּ לְהוּ בְּבַל תֹּאכַל חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1's inclusion of women in the חמץ prohibition and extends it to מצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in eating מצה, per רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's derivation that women must eat מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says women are obligated to eat מצה by Torah law. Because the verse links the two commands, whoever is forbidden to eat חמץ must also eat מצה, and women are forbidden to eat חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אליעזר said: women are obligated to eat מצה by Torah law, as it says 'Do not eat חמץ with it...'. Whoever is included in the prohibition of חמץ is included in eating מצה. These women too, since they are included in the prohibition of חמץ, are included in the command to eat מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר as the source for the conclusion it just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the two commands sitting side by side in one verse (דברים 16:3). רבי אליעזר reads the link in the direction 'חמץ → מצה': anyone bound by the prohibition is bound by the command. Since women are bound by the חמץ prohibition, they must eat מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (not just rabbinic)
Women are obligated
'Etc.': the verse continues

steps.confusionAlert: Step 1 read the link in one direction (מצה → חמץ) and step 3 reads it in the other (חמץ → מצה). Since women are definitely included in the חמץ prohibition, the link brings them into the מצה obligation.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Eliezer said:
Women are obligated in eating matzah
by Torah law,
as it is stated: "You shall not eat leavened bread with it, etc."
anyone who is included in "do not eat leaven"
is included in eating matzah.
And these women too,
since they are included in "do not eat leaven,"
they are included in "arise, eat matzah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for step 2's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That women are obligated to eat מצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's reading of the link between חמץ and מצה in דברים 16:3.
steps.whatToRemember: The prohibition of חמץ and the command of מצה are linked. Since women are included in the prohibition, רבי אליעזר holds they must eat מצה by Torah law.

steps.title: Why should the word כל include women and not mixtures of חמץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the use of the word כל to include women. Perhaps it comes to include a mixture containing חמץ (עירובו) in the punishment instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see to say that this word 'כל' comes to include women, and to leave out its mixture? Say instead that it comes to include its mixture!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier derivation: the extra word כל could just as easily teach something else, namely that a mixture with חמץ is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inclusive word like כל can only teach one extra thing. The גמרא asks why we spend it on women rather than on food that only contains חמץ mixed in. If כל is used for mixtures, we lose the source for including women in the חמץ prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this reading over another?
To include (as an extra case)
Its mixture: food with חמץ mixed into it
You take out / exclude

phrases.english: And what did you see
that this word "any" comes to include women,
and you exclude its mixture?
Say instead: it comes to include its mixture!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the derivation of women from the word כל and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of כל to include women in the חמץ prohibition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word could equally include a mixture of חמץ, so choosing women seems arbitrary.

steps.title: A verse about eaters adds eaters, not foods
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is more logical for כל to include women. The verse speaks about the people who eat, so its extra word should add more people, not more kinds of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable: the verse is talking about people who eat, so it adds more people who eat. Would a verse talking about people who eat add more things that are eaten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by looking at what the verse is about. The extra word fits women, who are more 'eaters', not mixtures, which are 'things eaten'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'כל אוכל חמץ', 'anyone who eats חמץ', so its subject is the person eating. An extra word should widen the same category the verse is discussing, which means more people. The closing line is a rhetorical question: of course a verse about eaters would not suddenly add kinds of food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / reasonable
It is dealing with / its subject is
Those who eat (people)
Things that are eaten (foods)

steps.whatToRemember: The word כל in 'כל אוכל חמץ' includes women, because a verse about eaters adds more eaters, not more kinds of food.

phrases.english: It is reasonable:
it is dealing with eaters, so it includes more eaters.
Would it deal with eaters and include more things that are eaten?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual logic: the inclusion must match the verse's subject
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כל might include mixtures of חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the verse speaks of eaters, כל includes more eaters, meaning women.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Women are included in the חמץ prohibition through the word כל, and therefore, per רבי אליעזר, they are obligated in מצה.

steps.title: רב נתן shows a verse about eaters that adds more foods
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן challenges the rule that a verse about eaters cannot add foods. In the ברייתא about חלב, the verse speaks about the one who eats, yet כי כל adds חלב of חולין animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן, the father of רב הונא, objected: Is it true that whenever a verse talks about the people who eat, it never adds more foods? A ברייתא teaches on the verse 'For anyone who eats the חלב of the animal from which one brings an offering': From this I would only know about חלב of unblemished animals that can be offered. How do I know about חלב of blemished animals? The verse says 'of the animal.' How do I know about חלב of חולין animals? The verse says 'for anyone.' This verse talks about eaters, yet it adds foods!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן attacks the reasoning from Step 5. He brings a ברייתא where a verse about eaters uses כי כל to add a new kind of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said that the כל in the חמץ verse adds people (women) rather than food (עירובו), because the verse speaks about eaters. The ברייתא shows the opposite pattern: the חלב verse also speaks about eaters, yet its כי כל adds חלב of חולין animals, which is a food. So the rule from Step 5 seems to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it, a sharp challenge
Those who eat, the people doing the eating
Things that are eaten, the foods
Forbidden fats of an animal
Blemished animals that cannot be brought as a קרבן
Ordinary animals that were never made holy

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up אוכלין (the eaters) with נאכלין (the foods). The whole argument depends on which of the two the extra word adds.

phrases.english: Rav Natan strongly objected to it
the father of Rav Huna (son of Rav Natan):
phrases.notes: The parentheses show a variant version of the name.

phrases.english: And anywhere that the verse deals with those who eat
does it not include foods?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
"For anyone who eats the fat of the animal
from which one brings an offering" (Vayikra 7:25)
I know only about the fat of unblemished animals
that are fit to be offered
From where do I know about the fat of blemished animals?
The verse says: "of the animal."
From where do I know about the fat of non-sacred animals?
The verse says: "for anyone."
But here the verse deals with those who eat,
and still it includes foods!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a verse about eaters adds only eaters, not foods
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: in the חלב verse, which speaks about eaters, כי כל adds חלב of חולין, a new food.

steps.title: Foods are added only when no extra eaters are available
steps.stepSummary: In the חלב case, there are no extra people left to add, so the verse adds foods. In the חמץ case, women can be added, so the verse adds them and does not switch to foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with חלב, there are no extra eaters to add, so the verse adds foods. Here, with חמץ, there are eaters to add, so the verse does not leave the eaters aside to add foods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב נתן by narrowing the rule. A verse about eaters first tries to add eaters, and it adds foods only when there are none left to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone is already forbidden to eat חלב, so there are no more people for כי כל to add, and it must add a food. With חמץ, women could have been exempt because of the link to מצה, so there are people to add. The extra word therefore stays on the subject of the verse, the eaters.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here, comparing the two cases
There is not / there is
It does not leave aside

steps.whatToRemember: An extra word adds things connected to the subject of its verse. It moves to a less connected subject only when nothing connected is left to add.

phrases.english: There, where there are no additional eaters,
it includes foods.
Here, where there are eaters to include,
it does not leave the eaters aside
and include foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נתן's challenge from Step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A verse about eaters can never add foods, so the חלב ברייתא contradicts the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding eaters comes first. A verse adds foods only when there are no extra eaters to add, as with חלב.

steps.title: How do the רבנן know women are forbidden to eat חמץ?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not hold that a mixture of חמץ is punishable, and they do not expound the word כל at all. So how do they know that women are included in the חמץ prohibition?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן, who do not hold that a mixture is included, do not expound the word כל. So where do they learn that women are included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first states a fact about the רבנן as a setup, then asks a question. If the רבנן don't expound כל, they have lost the source for including women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for women was the word כל. The רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר and do not include עירובו, which shows that they do not expound כל. But women surely are forbidden to eat חמץ, so the רבנן must have some other source.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
A mixture that contains חמץ
They expound, they learn a law from a word
From where do they know?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, who do not hold that a mixture is included,
do not expound "anything."
If so, from where do they know about women?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the view that expounds כל to the רבנן, who do not
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for including women according to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word כל was the source for women. The רבנן don't expound כל, so they seem to have no source.

steps.title: The רבנן learn from the longer phrase כי כל
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not expound the plain word כל, but they do expound the longer phrase כי כל. From it they learn that women are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not expound "כל." They do expound "כי כל."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן have a different source for women. They expound the fuller phrase כי כל in the חמץ verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word כל is not extra enough for the רבנן to learn from. The phrase כי כל, which appears in the verse 'כי כל אוכל חמץ,' is extra enough, and it teaches that women are included. This fits the חלב ברייתא from Step 6, which also learned from כי כל.

keyTerms.meaning: "For anyone", a longer and more extra phrase than כל alone

steps.whatToRemember: Even the רבנן, who do not expound the plain word כל, agree that women are forbidden to eat חמץ. They learn it from the fuller phrase כי כל.

phrases.english: "Anything" they do not expound;
"For anyone" they do expound.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the רבנן don't expound כל, they have no source for women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן expound כי כל, and from it they include women.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי אליעזר split the two words between women and the mixture?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר does not learn women from כל and the mixture of חמץ from כי כל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אליעזר, let us say: 'כל' comes to include the women, and 'כי כל' comes to include a mixture of חמץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר. Since כי כל can be expounded, he could split the two expressions: כל includes women, and the extra כי כל includes a mixture of חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that it is more logical for כל to include women, since the verse is about the people who eat. We also learned that the longer phrase כי כל can be expounded. So רבי אליעזר, who uses כל for women, should also use the extra כי כל to make one who eats עירובו liable to כרת. Why doesn't he?

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who expounds the word כל and includes a mixture of חמץ in the prohibition
Let us say (suggesting a different reading)
To include (an extra word adds something)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Eliezer, say:
'Any' comes to include the women,
'For any' comes to include its mixture!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 9 (that כי כל is expounded) and the logic of step 5 (כל should add people) to question רבי אליעזר's method.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's failure to include עירובו in the חמץ verse, even though it contains the extra phrase כי כל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כל includes women and the fuller phrase כי כל can also be expounded, רבי אליעזר should learn women from כל and עירובו from כי כל.

steps.title: Proof that רבי אליעזר does expound כי כל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the answer that רבי אליעזר does not expound כי כל. It brings a ברייתא about שאור on the מזבח that expounds both כל and כי כל, and that ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that רבי אליעזר does not expound 'כי כל', wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'You shall not burn שאור on the מזבח.' From this I know only a whole piece. From where do I know part of it? The verse says 'כל'. From where do I know its mixture? The verse says 'כי כל'. Whom have we heard who expounds 'כל'? רבי אליעזר. And here he expounds 'כי כל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first raises a possible defense: maybe רבי אליעזר does not expound כי כל at all. It then knocks down that defense with a ברייתא, which makes the question from step 10 even stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about burning שאור on the מזבח learns 'part of it' from כל and 'its mixture' from כי כל. Only רבי אליעזר expounds the word כל, so this ברייתא must follow him. That shows רבי אליעזר does expound כי כל, so he should have done the same with the חמץ verse.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא raises a possible answer in order to reject it)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (introduces a contradicting source)
Do not burn leaven (sourdough) on the מזבח
Part of it
Whom have you heard who holds this? (identifies the author of an unnamed source)

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about offering שאור on the מזבח. It is not about eating חמץ on פסח. The גמרא brings it only to show how רבי אליעזר reads the words כל and כי כל.

phrases.english: And if you will say that 'for any'
Rabbi Eliezer does not expound,
but wasn't it taught: 'Leaven you shall not burn' —
I would only know a whole piece,
from where do we know part of it?
phrases.notes: Part of a piece of leaven

phrases.english: The verse says: 'any.'
From where do we know its mixture?
The verse says: 'for any.'
Whom have you heard who expounds 'any'?
Rabbi Eliezer, and here he expounds 'for any'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא ״כִּי כׇּל״ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא דָּרֵישׁ, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense of רבי אליעזר and so makes the challenge of step 10 stronger.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר does expound the phrase כי כל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שאור בל תקטירו that learns מקצתו from כל and עירובו from כי כל. It is attributed to רבי אליעזר because he is the one who expounds כל.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the challenge against רבי אליעזר without an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer. The question from steps 10 and 11 stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קשיא means the problem is real and unsolved. It does not mean רבי אליעזר's opinion is rejected. We simply do not know why he does not learn the mixture from כי כל in the חמץ verse.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: the question stands unanswered, but the opinion is not rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא could not explain why רבי אליעזר, who does expound כי כל elsewhere, does not use it for the חמץ mixture. The question remains a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: A קשיא is not a תיובתא. A תיובתא knocks down an opinion. A קשיא only leaves a question open.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of steps 10 and 11 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge to רבי אליעזר's derivation remains unresolved.

steps.title: A permitted food does not join a forbidden food, except for a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי יוחנן: in all Torah prohibitions, permitted food does not join forbidden food to reach the minimum amount for punishment. The only exception is a נזיר, because of the word משרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In all the prohibitions of the Torah, a permitted food does not join together with a forbidden food, except for the prohibitions of a נזיר, because the Torah said 'משרת' (anything soaked).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new, related rule about mixtures. רבי יוחנן says that a permitted food never counts toward the minimum amount of a forbidden food, except for a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be punished, a person must eat a minimum amount (usually a כזית) of the forbidden food. If he eats a bit of forbidden food mixed with permitted food, the permitted part does not count toward that amount. A נזיר is different, because the Torah forbids him even food soaked in wine (משרת). This shows that for a נזיר, the permitted food joins with the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: A permitted food joins with a forbidden food to make up the minimum amount
A person who vowed not to drink wine or eat grape products
Anything soaked (in grapes or wine), from the verse about the נזיר
An אמורא who transmits teachings of רבי יוחנן

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the coming discussion about mixtures. The גמרא will ask how far the נזיר exception goes and whether other prohibitions follow the same pattern.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
In all the prohibitions in the Torah,
a permitted food does not join with a forbidden food,
except for the prohibitions of a nazirite,
for the Torah said: 'soaked.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of a חמץ mixture, the גמרא brings a general rule about mixing permitted and forbidden foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Torah prohibitions, permitted food does not join forbidden food to reach the minimum amount for punishment. The exception is a נזיר, derived from the word משרת.

steps.title: זעירי adds שאור on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: זעירי says that the prohibition of offering שאור on the מזבח is also a case where permitted food joins forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And זעירי said: also the prohibition 'do not burn שאור' on the מזבח is a case where permitted and forbidden combine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, זעירי, adds a second exception to רבי יוחנן's rule. According to him, the rule that permitted food joins forbidden food applies to שאור on the מזבח too, not only to a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said נזיר was the only exception. זעירי says the prohibition of offering שאור on the מזבח is another one. So if someone offers a mixture of שאור and permitted flour, the permitted part counts toward the minimum amount for punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who adds a case to the list
Also / even, adding a new case
Sourdough (leavening agent), forbidden to offer on the מזבח
The prohibition 'you shall not burn' (Vayikra 2:11)

steps.confusionAlert: זעירי agrees with the basic idea of רבי יוחנן's rule, but he does disagree about its scope: רבי יוחנן said נזיר is the only exception, and זעירי adds שאור on the מזבח as another.

phrases.english: And Ze'eiri said:
Also the prohibition of 'do not burn leaven' [is a case where permitted joins forbidden].
phrases.notes: Refers to ויקרא 2:11: כי כל שאור וכל דבש לא תקטירו

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exception to רבי יוחנן's rule, which said נזיר was the only one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For offering שאור on the מזבח, the permitted part of a mixture joins the forbidden part to reach the minimum amount.

steps.title: Whose opinion does זעירי follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא זעירי's ruling is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did זעירי say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question: which earlier sage does זעירי's ruling follow? This question sets up the answer that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting a mixture of שאור as a punishable offering needs a source in the פסוק. The גמרא wants to find which תנא reads the פסוק that way.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (asks which sage a ruling follows)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind זעירי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view זעירי's ruling follows.

steps.title: זעירי follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: זעירי follows רבי אליעזר, who expounds the word כל to include mixtures.
steps.simpleTranslation: He follows רבי אליעזר, who expounds the word 'כל' (all).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that זעירי follows רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר learns from the word כל that a mixture also counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 11, the גמרא identified the ברייתא about שאור on the מזבח as רבי אליעזר's, because he is the one who expounds inclusive words like כל. זעירי's extra exception for שאור on the מזבח fits רבי אליעזר's method of expounding these words, so the גמרא attributes זעירי's ruling to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Who expounds, who learns a lesson from a word
'All', the word expounded to include mixtures

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי's extra exception (שאור on the מזבח) depends on רבי אליעזר's reading of the word כל.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer,
who expounds the word 'all'.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק כי כל שאור

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זעירי follows רבי אליעזר, who expounds כל to include a mixture.

steps.title: If so, a challenge begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge to the idea that זעירי follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. The words 'if so' signal that a challenge is coming, and the challenge itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has just tied זעירי to רבי אליעזר's reading of כל. Now it will ask what problem follows from that link. The actual content of the challenge appears in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, an opening formula for a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the opening of the question. Do not look for the full challenge here, because it continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: If so,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge to the answer given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that זעירי follows רבי אליעזר's reading of כל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If זעירי follows רבי אליעזר, the גמרא will show that something more should follow from this. The details continue on the next amud.
